（印：刑第三科長）

Further enquiries made at the Swiss Consulate ascertained that the three years old female child as mentioned in the preceding diaries is recognised as an American and registered in the Consulate as Carol A. Sanborn. The Foh Sing Flour Mill who was then taking temporary care of the child requested the Consulate to make necessary arrangements as to the disposal of this child.

Mr. Croset of the Swiss Consulate has been communicated with and he agreed to accept the child into the Consulate's care pending further instructions from the H.I.J.M. Consulate. At 4 p.m. 27-4-43 this child was taken to the Swiss Consulate and Mr. Croset in turn sent her to St. Joseph's Convent, French Concession pending instructions from the Japanese Authorities.

（印：刑特受 18.4.43 受）

（印：刑特第三科）

On 27-3-43 an inquest was held in the public
Mortuary on the body of the deceased when the
following verdict was handed down by Procurator
Hsia Sei Sung:-
"Death due to fire burns. Body to be
removed by the representative from
Foh Sing Flour Mill, named Chu Zai
Yee, for burial."

On 30-3-43 Mr. H. Buergin of the Swiss Consulate
came to station and requested the assistance of police
to visit the 3 years old child, as mentioned in the
first diary, who is now under the temporary care of
Mr. Szé Poh Hou (史復候), assistant manager of the
Foh Sing Flour Mill. Necessary assistance was rendered
and Mr. Buergin stated that he will make arrangements
with Japanese Authorities to send the child to camp to
stay with the father James Gordon Sanborn. He will inform
the Police before the child is taken away.

Pontoo Road
Misc. 36/43
March 26 1943.

Death of A Female Chinese who
Married to an American.

Sir:-
At 11:40 p.m. 25-3-43 a telephone message was
received at the station from St. Elizabeth's Hospital,
Avenue Road reporting that a female Chinese had been
admitted from No. 5 West Soochow Road and detained in
the hospital suffering from burning.

Enquiries revealed that the injured person, namely,
Dao Ai Lee (陶愛麗), 37, soochow,
m/female, No. 5 West Soochow Road,
known as Mrs. Allie Sanborn.

was knitting some woollen article in her quarters at the
Foh Sing Flour Mill No. 2 at No. 5 West Soochow Road at
about 10 p.m. 25-3-43 when her evening gown caught fire
from a nearby electric heater and simultaneously spreaded
all over her clothing. She raised an alarm and a mill
coolie Woo Ah Foh (吳阿福) responded to and managed to
extinguish the fire on her clothing. However, she had
then been badly burned and was immediately conveyed to
St. Elizabeth's Hospital for treatment as afore-mentioned.
Dr.'s chit:-"Burn, 2nd degree, entire body."

At 7 a.m. 26/3/43 St. Elizabeth's Hospital telephoned
to the station and reported that the above mentioned
injured female had died at 3.30 a.m. 26/3/43. Death
Certificate:- "Admitted with 2nd degree burn of whole
body, died at 3.30 a.m. 26/3/43."

Further enquiries revealed that the now deceased
was married to an American named James Gordon Sanborn,
age 78, head miller of Foh Sing Flour Mill No.2 & 8 West
Soochow Road. They lived together in the quarters on the
mill premises. On 3/3/43 J.G. Sanborn reported to the
concentration camp and since then the now deceased lived

in the quarters alone with her 3 years old daughter.
Mr. Wurster of the Swiss Consulate (now taking care of the
American affairs) was communicated with who stated that though the
now deceased was married to an American she was not recognised as an
American citizen. She was in possession of a Chinese C.C. No.76134
issued by Pootoo Road District. The now deceased has no relative
or close friend in Shanghai and the 3 years old daughter is now
temporary under the care of the Foh Sing Flour Mill. Mr. Wurster
further stated that there is no record in the Swiss Consulate
regarding this child but he requested a copy of this report be
supplied to him so as he will communicate with her father who is
now in concentration camp as to the child's disposal.
Japanese Gendarmerie, Gordon Road Branch, informed.
Body of the now deceased had been removed to Public Mortuary
pending an inquest to be held a.m. 27/3/43 when representative of
the Foh Sing Flour Mill, Mr. Chu Zai Yee (朱才怡), will attend to
take care of the burial of the body.
Foul play not suspected.
